quest.title: Final Stanza: The Sanctification of Tao Dou
quest.description: Thanks to everyone's efforts, the border crisis has finally been resolved. It seems that Xiangling has something she wants to talk to you about in Liyue Harbor...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, hey Xiangling! What's up?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: You know what's up! Our get-together, of course!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ah, yes, finally time for that meal.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Yeah! You are free, right? You are not getting out of this without a very good reason!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're not the ones who held it up! That was Hu Tao!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Yeah, tell me about it... She thinks being a director gives her a license to be a flake. It's like, unless there's a sizeable crowd coming, it's not worth my time.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: But don't worry — we've agreed that this time, we're not gonna accept any more excuses from her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? Who's "we"?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Hehe, Xingqiu and I! He said he's been wanting to invite everyone out for a long time, but given the situation with his great-grandfather, he never had the time.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: But amazingly, on the night of the Lantern Rite, his great-grandfather suddenly woke up! Xingqiu was thrilled — and he was finally able to leave the house. So we met up right away and made a plan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! So his great-grandfather's gonna be alright?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Yep! They had a doctor take a look and everything. He'll be just fine.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: According to Xingqiu, his great-grandfather has been eating like Paimon since he woke up... so now, the family's biggest worry is that he'll get indigestion.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Well, that's good news, but somehow doesn't paint Paimon in the best light...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Don't worry, it definitely does! Your appetite represents an optimistic outlook on life: "Always eat to your heart's content, lest your chopsticks wither with regret"!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well said, Xiangling! Yeah, that attitude is exactly what got Paimon to where she is today!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: For real? How come I'm only hearing this for the first time?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yes, for real! Like Xiangling said, always eat till your heart's content, and don't let your chopsticks... um, what was it?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Haha, don't worry. Save it for the dinner table, Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, no problem! But where are we gonna eat?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: At Yilong Wharf, later tonight! Xingqiu and the others are still out there. Oh, and Hu Tao said that we'll be joined by a special guest!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who is it?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: You'll see when you get there!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh! Paimon has an idea... But, she'll keep it to herself for now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I have an idea, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Who?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm keeping it to myself, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph! Well, we'll see who guessed right later tonight!

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: If we're talking the strongest... I'd have to pick Wind Reader. After all, he was the founding master of Qimen Divination.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Yeah! He gets my vote too, being my ancestor and everything. Oh, and also the silver swallow!

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: In that case, I'd have to nominate the Two Sages of Lianshan. It's always the ones who live in seclusion and never show their skill who turn out to be the most powerful of all. Well, in the books, anyway. What do you think?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: If this were a martial arts novel, then I'd agree with you.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: But unfortunately, after reading "Moonlit Bamboo Forest," I am convinced that the title should go to the White Horse of the Three Immortals of Tao Dou. She's got to be hiding some kind of secret.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Huh? Is no one gonna pick the Yunlai Angler? Even the Yuheng said that her sword-fighting style comes from the Yunlai Angler's rod-wielding techniques.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Yeah, so they say... But I mean, fishing? Just seems kinda lame in this context...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Hmm... Although it's more common than you might think for anglers to be more than what they seem.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hey, you're all wrong! The greatest of all were obviously Old Man Wuwang and the Lone Butterfly. Without them, there'd be no Wangsheng Funeral Parlor today.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: Hard to argue with that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, everyone's here already!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, you're finally here! Welcome!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! Hu Tao, your hat!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Well noticed, Paimon. Yes, I added another plum branch.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Ooh! So now you and {NICKNAME} have matching plum branches.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But um, anyway, what are you all up to?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: We're debating who's the best out of the Eight Adepts.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Hahaha, well kind of. An open-ended debate, maybe. We're just shooting the breeze really.

dialogues.speaker: Chongyun
dialogues.text: That's right. The only way you could settle a question like this would be with those special goggles they have in light novels, where you can read someone's power level just by looking at them.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Haha, has Xingqiu been getting you into light novels?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: #Welcome, {NICKNAME}. My family tell me that you and Hu Tao performed a very risky ceremony, and cured great-grandfather's illness in the process.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: I cannot thank you enough for your efforts. No matter what kind of trouble you may encounter in the future, you will always find a helping hand at the Feiyun Commerce Guild.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It was a team effort.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Yeah, I know. My father and brother will thank everyone individually in the coming days.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Why go to all that trouble, Xingqiu? Save yourself the effort and just admit to me, here and now, that the strongest of the Eight Adepts are the Lone Butterfly and Old Man Wuwang! Then we'll be square.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Come on, enough with the debate already! Everyone's here now, so let's eat.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Paimon, you're up! It's time to share your grand philosophy of life with everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... O—Okay, umm... One sec... It's like, always eat to your heart's content, lest your... what was the rest, again?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Lest your chopsticks wither in regret.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahh, right, right! Yeah, that's it!

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Whoa, Paimon, you can't stumble through a motto you live by! It's bad luck! It'll make your life full of stumbling blocks too. Come on, you can do it! One more time, from the top!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Always eat to your heart's content! Lest your chopsticks wither in regret!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's the spirit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, is it time to dig in now?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Paimon, did you forget about our special guest?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right! Paimon remembers now. Actually, Paimon guessed who it is already, but y'know, no point in saying it out loud or anything...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hmm? You don't sound confident... You don't have a clue who it is, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Ugh, yes, actually! It's obvious who it is. It's, you-know-who, um... {NICKNAME}, a little help!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is it Yun Jin?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Correct! It's our very own Yun Jin. So you haven't forgotten what she said last time.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Look, she's taking the stage.

dialogues.speaker: Lixing
dialogues.text: Whoa! Isn't that the director of the Yun-Han Opera Troupe?

dialogues.speaker: Jiewu
dialogues.text: Amazing! I never would've expected to see her all the way out here in Yilong Wharf.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Greetings, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: I will perform "The Sanctification of Tao Dou" one more time, for all my friends who were unable to join the festivities during the Lantern Rite. My apologies for not being able to set up a grander stage.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aww, that's so nice! She's doing a whole new performance for everyone who couldn't attend last time!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Shh! She's about to begin.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Recall the bold claims about Tao Dou

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Through discordant tones and tragic fates, souls of two worlds, heed my call

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: What delusions thou hast, to set the realm flame with bones and blood

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Shadows of war shall fade with time, while tales of salvation will ever live on

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Sins must be paid once blood is spilled, the rules of life and death thou cannot confront

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: The ways of heaven shall ever point true, while selfish desires will lead to your doom

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Pledges were made to vanquish evil, eight Adepts raised their blades against Tao Dou

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Though the body is spent and soul washed away, dreams and ways will continue always

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Swallows will return for a new nest, just as tears and branches will commemorate the day

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: #You should have gone with {NICKNAME} into the border that day.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: #I get that you care about {NICKNAME}'s wellbeing. But the fact is, it wouldn't have helped. I'd have just been an extra liability if something went wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Besides, Ningguang changed the plan and sent me to The Chasm instead. I can't be in two places at once.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: If you're not happy about it, why don't you file a complaint at Yujing Terrace?

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Hmph... and report the Tianquan to the Tianquan?

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Actually, I was thinking the Yuheng. She's not afraid of a confrontation.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: ...Forget it. I'll let it go since everyone's fine.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Heh. Wangshu Inn is a fine location...

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: All of Liyue is a fine location.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Haha, well said.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Boss, another serving of Dew-Dipped Shrimp please, with some dipping spices.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: ...And one Almond Tofu.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Hey, the crisis is resolved. Why the long face, Tianquan?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: #Thanks to Director Hu and {NICKNAME}, disaster was averted. But we still do not know what caused the crisis in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: I know you are well-informed, Captain. So I trust you are aware that the nation of Natlan has recently endured some major events relating to the Ley Lines and to issues of life and death.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: It makes me wonder whether these events might somehow be connected on a deeper level.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: If they are, then this'll be bigger than just Liyue and Natlan. I'll send word to my business partners, and keep an eye out for any similar incidents in the other nations.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Right now, though... I say, put those worries to one side and focus on enjoying these stunning sights before they disappear for another year.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Hehe, but of course. You don't need to teach me about work-life balance — I am no Keqing.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Is that right? Well then, why are you still wearing that same old hairpin? Didn't I tell you to use my pay to buy yourself a new one?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: I wouldn't dare touch Captain Beidou's Mora without final confirmation. What if you'd been speaking in jest? I'd never hear the end of it.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Hahaha, do I really have to go pick one out for you? Alright, suits me. Let's go take a stroll through the fair.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Well done... When did our straight-talking Captain learn to read between the lines, hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Hahaha, that's enough. Are you coming or not?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Why not? Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Still working, Ganyu? Sorry it's been so busy.

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: #Huh? Oh, Keqing... No, it's fine, nothing out of the ordinary. {NICKNAME} and Director Hu are the real stars this year.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: That's no reason to diminish your own contribution. Of course they were the biggest heroes...

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: But we played our part, and played it well. The Ministry of Civil Affairs responded at record speed, did we not?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Even though on the surface, this incident looks negligible compared to the disasters of the Archon War, it was a very close call. Things could have been unimaginably worse had we not found a solution.

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: You're right... Actually, I have a question about the Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method we ended up using. How come I've never seen any records of it in the Yuehai Pavilion before?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Oh, you want to know about the origins of the array? Ningguang made the whole thing up.

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: Haha. I'm joking.

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: In truth, a letter with all the critical information suddenly appeared in Yujing Terrace on the day when we needed it. Even Yelan was unable to track down where it had come from.

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: Wait... the info just appeared out of thin air? Then... wasn't that a bit of a risky strategy on Ningguang's part...?

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: It may appear that way, but if you think about it carefully, everything slowly starts to make sense...

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: How many people in all of Liyue could know about both the crisis and the secret art, while also possessing the ability to deliver a letter without leaving a trace?

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: Ah... You mean... Master and her friends?

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: I see.

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: That young lass from the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor is rather impressive.

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: One's curiosity was piqued when Rex Lapis chose to serve as her consultant. But only now does one understand the true intent behind his decision.

dialogues.speaker: Moon Carver
dialogues.text: Agreed. And yet, what a rare delight it is to hear such effusive praise from you, Cloud Retainer.

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: "Rare"? Pray elaborate a little further.

dialogues.speaker: Mountain Shaper
dialogues.text: In the past, you may have uttered something to the tune of this: "Though the lass displays a measure of talent, it is nothing more than Shenhe or Ganyu could have achieved if placed in the same circumstances."

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: Hmph! One would never deride others as a means of praising one's own children. The Wangsheng lass displayed great determination and fortitude. Does that not make her deserving of a few words of praise?

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Hehehe, it certainly does. And she is not the first. I've lived in Liyue Harbor for a long time now, and I can tell you that the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor has produced generation upon generation of outstanding directors.

dialogues.speaker: Moon Carver
dialogues.text: Streetward Rambler speaks true. The god Tao Dou was not our friend, but neither was he our enemy. Had he not cared greatly for all living things, and volunteered to sanctify himself to pacify the underworld...

dialogues.speaker: Moon Carver
dialogues.text: Not even eight adepti would have been able to overpower him, much less the eight adepts. When he became the border, he likely never imagined that mortals would preserve and maintain his new form this far into the future...

dialogues.speaker: Mountain Shaper
dialogues.text: With all of that said, I realize the name of the young lady from the funeral parlor is still unknown to me.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: The Director's surname is Hu, and her given name is Tao.

dialogues.speaker: Moon Carver
dialogues.text: Hu... Ah! As in, our word for "butterfly," yes?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: No, Hu as in "mischief-maker."

dialogues.speaker: Moon Carver
dialogues.text: Then "Tao" must likewise be the "Tao" that means mischief in our tongue?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: No, in fact, it is the same Tao as appears in "Tao Dou."

dialogues.speaker: Mountain Shaper
dialogues.text: Ah. So "Hu" as in butterfly, and "Tao" as in "Tao Dou." A fine name. Fitting indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: No, Hu as in "mischief-maker," "incessant pestering," and "wonton gluttony"!

dialogues.speaker: Mountain Shaper
dialogues.text: I say, I was merely trying to liven up the mood. Why is Hu Tao permitted to make mischief while I am not?

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: Hah! The clue is in the name. If you wish to change yours from Mountain Shaper to Mischief Maker, be my guest.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Hehe, why not have some tea? This is the rare "Spirit Sprout" cultivar that Rex Lapis brought back all the way back from Qingce Village. It'd be a shame to miss out.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: May there be more good tea to share in the coming year.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: I am sure there shall be.
